one_month_reasoning: Scheduled events in the 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-29 window: the FOMC decision on Oct 28 (meeting Oct 27-28; corrected from Oct 29 per the supervisor), where Kalshi/Polymarket priced ~69% odds of a second consecutive 25bp hike as of Sep 29 (defirate/CNBC; volume not reachable). Because the hike is largely priced, it adds variance more than drift; a hawkish surprise (e.g. signalling more hikes) is the main downside tail, as on Sep 16 when ON fell 9% alongside the analyst day. onsemi's Q3 report is still only estimated for ~Nov 2 (MarketBeat; onsemi's IR site returned 503 when I tried to confirm), i.e. most likely just outside the window, with a small chance it lands earlier or is pre-announced. Peer Q3 prints (TXN, NXPI, STM) in late October will move analog/auto semis. Short-horizon regularities are mixed: strongly negative 3-month momentum (down ~44% from the June 3 high) vs a ~14% bounce off the Sep 16 low. No directional edge, so I center at $75.95 with ~16% monthly sigma (slightly below 64%/3.5 = 18% because the realized figure is inflated by two one-off event days).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (horizon NTM EPS ~$4.50 x 17.5x = $78.75, weight 0.5), 2027 EPS on a consensus haircut ($4.10 x 19x = $78, weight 0.25) and FCF yield on normalised capex (~$1.7B 2027 FCF = ~$4.30/share at 5.5% = $78, weight 0.25) -> ~$78.

inputs_detail.derivation: CY27 consensus $4.53 (30 analysts, stockanalysis; BofA $4.57); NTM at Sep-2027 blends 2027/2028 (~$5.0 standalone) and I haircut ~10% for a Fed hiking cycle and Synaptics dilution (~13.6% more ON shares, partly offset by $200M synergies).

ON 10-yr median trailing P/E ~22x (GuruFocus); BofA uses 20x 2028 EPS; ON currently ~16.8x CY27. Raised from 17x: the round-1 discount for a stock-merger drag was over-applied, since Savor-Lu find completed stock acquirers outperform failed ones and the drag concentrates in overvalued acquirers, and ON has already de-rated ~44%. Still a discount to history for integration risk and rising rates.
Consensus $4.53 cut ~10%: Q3 guide midpoint $0.87 and Q2 $0.74 imply 2026 ~$3.20; reaching $4.53 needs ~41% growth, and consensus in cyclical recoveries under rate hikes has historically overshot.
Slight premium to the NTM multiple because it is on a nearer-year EPS; below ON's long-run median ~22x.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2027 FCF ~$1.7B (normalised capex ~5% of revenue) / ~395M diluted shares = ~$4.30/share, 5.5% yield

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 2026 FCF $425M flattered by trough capex ($34.3M in Q2, $56.2M in H1, ~2% of revenue, per the Q2 8-K and supervisor check). On ~$7.2B 2027 revenue (consensus $7.42B, lightly haircut), ~29% operating cash flow margin less ~5% capex (management model) gives ~24% FCF margin = ~$1.7B, down from my round-1 $1.9B.
Q3 2026 non-GAAP diluted share guidance (pre-Synaptics; the deal is expected to close mid-2027 and is treated as roughly per-share neutral within the horizon).
Fed hiked in September and ~69% odds of another hike Oct 28, so a higher yield than 2021-era levels; cyclical semis at 5%+ FCF yield usually sit at trough-to-mid valuations.

bear.story: Fed keeps hiking into a slowdown, auto/industrial recovery stalls, Chinese SiC price pressure hits margins, Synaptics integration/dilution weigh; EPS ~$3.5 at ~13-14x; revisits the 2025 lows.

base.story: Recovery continues (AI data center ramp, utilisation and GM up toward 40-42%), EPS ~$4.1-4.5, FCF ~$1.7B once capex normalises, multiple ~17-19x while the market waits for the 2028-2030 payoff; Synaptics closes mid-2027.

bull.story: Cycle upturn plus AI power wins re-rate ON toward 24-25x on ~$5 NTM EPS; rates peak; completed deal is received better than feared (consistent with completed stock acquirers outperforming failed ones) and the stock recovers much of the gap to the June high of $134.92.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$51 the stock would trade at ~11-12x CY27 consensus EPS ($4.53) and ~13x my haircut EPS, and ~8% yield on normalised FCF (~$1.7B), levels ON only reached near the 2025 cycle trough. Getting there would most likely require a real guidance cut (auto/industrial demand relapse, SiC price war hitting device margins, utilisation reversal) or a failed/renegotiated Synaptics deal, not ordinary ~50-60% vol noise.

reasoning: Base-rate anchoring: ON is a high-beta cyclical (64% realized vol, 10-yr trailing P/E median ~22x) that has fallen ~44% from its June 3 high of $134.92 on two events: a 24% one-day drop on the ~$7B all-stock Synaptics deal (Jun 25) and a 9% drop on the Sep 16 analyst day coinciding with a Fed hike. Its prior 2023-2025 drawdown was ~-40% and bottomed when expectations reset. Round 2 changes: (1) the supervisor showed my FCF leg capitalised trough capex (Q2 capex $34.3M, ~2% of sales); normalising capex toward ~5% cuts 2027 FCF from $1.9B to ~$1.7B and that leg from $87 to $78. (2) On the supervisor's prompt I re-checked the stock-merger base rate: Savor-Lu (2009) actually find completed stock acquirers outperform failed ones and that the negative effect concentrates in overvalued acquirers; Loughran-Vijh's average drag is real but ON has already de-rated ~44% to ~16.8x CY27, so I judge it largely priced and removed the extra merger discount from the multiple (17x -> 17.5x). Net fair value moves $80 -> ~$78. (3) FOMC decision date corrected to Oct 28; it is inside the 1-month window but ~69% priced. Fundamentals otherwise unchanged: Q2 revenue +9% y/y, non-GAAP GM 39.3% guided to 40-42%, net debt ~$0.6B, CY27 consensus $4.53, mean target ~$104. The two changes offset in the distribution (lower FCF value vs less merger drag), so I keep the median near $78.5 with ~52% lognormal sigma plus slightly fatter tails, giving P(>=76) ~0.525; bear 25% near $48, bull 25% near $122. I disagree with nothing material in the supervisor's file; my EPS haircut (~10%) remains a judgment call it left open. Research was limited: onsemi IR returned 503, so the Q3 date is still an estimate.

Supervisor asked whether the stock-merger drag is already priced; Savor-Lu find the drag concentrates in overvalued acquirers and completed deals beat failed ones, and ON has de-rated ~44%, so I removed part of the merger discount.
Net of the lower FCF leg and the slightly higher P/E multiple.
